reason: The drag-link eyes are modelled smaller than the part the design names. The model and row describe 'O9 eyes on 2 x MR63ZZ', but the model samples them as O8 discs (EYE_R = 4.0, model line 51, used in _disc(..., EYE_R) and in the horn's reach r_h + EYE_R). The arm tip's own eye at c1 is not sampled as a disc at all, only as the 6 mm strap. Worn here with EYE_R = 4.5 set in memory only (model unchanged, verifier harness, exact Bench(110,360)): the claim moves 22.64 -> 22.76 and the corrected number 97.83 -> 97.95 (in-band 0.8638 -> 0.8626), +0.12 points. Small, and it does not change any ranking.

No spring-return or dynamics number exists for this drive. The dog is one-sided: link 2's flank pushes the sector only while K opens. On the way back, K's spiral spring (the lead's) has to back-drive horn -> drag link -> Ti arm -> sector through the 4R. It works against the sector's turn on hub 2's housing and 4 MR63ZZ, with transmission angles down to 54.5 deg (pa_max_taken 35.5 deg; table end at PA 42). If the return lags, K lags q2 and the cuff twists or the chain binds (G3). Nothing on file measures it: no R17 / judge/dynamics.py run and no CAD for this design. The row's 'R17 ok' covers only static determinacy (with K on stop A, the 4R parks the ring). This is the same open measurement as the lead's M5, which its skeptic upheld as missing.
